text.tspan: Rat artwork modified from "A black rat sitting upright on the ground" by W.S. Wellcome, used under CC BY 4.0
pax rodentia is a distortion effect derived from the infamous ProCo RAT 2.
op-amp rodent distortion | op-amp based output buffer
3-way diode clipping control | true germanium diodes
internally adjustable Ruetz mod ("Mode B") | alternative tone stack design
The clipping amplifier stage uses the OP07 chip, as in the ProCo RAT 2.
A mode switch is provided that toggles on the "Ruetz mod" into the circuit
when set to B, reducing the gain and bringing more low end into the
output signal. (The character of mode B is internally adjustable).
Three clipping options are provided: 2x 1N4148 silicon diodes,
2x red LEDs, or 2x genuine 1N34A germanium diodes.
Additionally, there is the option to bring in another 1N4148 silicon diode
for subtle asymmetrical clipping in all three modes.
The typical filter control has been exchanged for an alternative
design modified from the "Simply Wonderful Tone Stack 3"
The output buffer (typically JFET-based) has been replaced with an
(The amount of recovery gain is internally adjustable).
